validity.recommendation: No action needed on existence/classification. This is a real, distinct entity (GEM's own OtherLanguagePrimaryPipelineName tags it '2-ая нитка' = '2nd string'), not a phantom row -- see the separate spec/attribution entries below for value-level problems.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: CONFIRMED, independent of GEM/its wiki mirror. Intergas Central Asia's own official site (https://intergas.kz/ru/obwaya-informaciya/, verified live) lists 'МГ «Бухарский Газоносный Район – ташкент-бишкек-алматы»' as an actively operated trunk system under three of its own regional directorates (УМГ Шымкент, УМГ Тараз, УМГ Алматы). Separately and more specifically, a distinct capacity-expansion/reconstruction project on this exact corridor's Kyrgyz section is independently, concretely documented by THREE separate outlets covering the 2016-2017 works: neftegaz.ru (trade press, 2017-08-29, verified live -- states Gazprom commissioned the newly built '2nd stage' (2-я очередь) of the 'бухарский газоносный район - ташкент - бишкек - алматы' pipeline running from the Kazakh-Kyrgyz border to the Sokuluk compressor station, and states that after ALSO reconstructing the existing '1st stage' section, throughput at the Chuy metering point on the Kyrgyz Republic's territory rose to almost double, to 3.9 bcm/y -- an EXACT match, to the decimal, of this row's Capacity value); ru.sputnik.kg (2017-08-29, verified live, corroborates independently: the pipeline from Tashkent to Almaty via Kyrgyzstan was launched, with 111 km of reconstructed mainline through Kyrgyzstan and a post-upgrade capacity of 1.7 bcm/y for that reconstructed stretch); and vesti.kg (2017-04-05, verified live, describes construction starting October 2016, with the 2nd-stage Kyrgyz segment spanning corridor km-posts 1001-1063 and the 1st-stage spanning km-posts 1063-1113, i.e. a combined ~112 km, not the full 1,585 km corridor). So a real 2016-2017 capacity-expansion project on this corridor's Kyrgyz section genuinely exists and is well corroborated by 3 independent outlets -- this row is not a hallucination. Classification (transmission gas trunk, Fuel=Gas) is consistent across every source and matches the sibling row P0739 ('Line I').

validity.recommendation: Do NOT delete or merge this row into P0739 -- it is a distinct, real entity. But its LengthKnown=1585.00 km and StartYear1=1999 are unsupported by any live independent source and are internally inconsistent with the row's own, well-matched Capacity=3.9 value (which is exactly the 2017-vintage post-upgrade Chuy-station throughput figure, per neftegaz.ru). Route to Update: (a) re-source Length/StartYear1/Diameter off the dead library.tou.edu.kz PDF; (b) resolve what 'Line II' is actually meant to span -- the corridor-wide route NF drew (RouteType=Mapped, RouteAccuracy=high, RouteNotes='parallel to Pipeline I') implies a full 1,585 km second parallel string, but the only concrete, independently verifiable event tied to this row's numbers (the exact 3.9 bcm/y Capacity match) describes a ~112 km Kyrgyz-section reconstruction project completed 2017, not a full second corridor-length pipe finished in 1999. These two framings cannot both be literally true of one entity; a human needs to decide which one this row represents and correct the mismatched fields (most likely Length and StartYear1, since Capacity is the best-evidenced field on the row).
validity.researcher_notes: Ran down the current citation first: Start [ref], Diameter [ref], and FuelSource [ref] all point to the SAME URL, https://library.tou.edu.kz/fulltext/bibl/b794.pdf ('Газопроводы Казахстана', Jan 2013). I re-verified this myself independently of the sweep's automated check: `curl -sk` (bypassing the known incomplete TLS chain, per the standing SOP note on adilet-style KZ .kz certs) returns a genuine, non-TLS-related HTTP 404 Not Found (Apache/PHP error page, 1.3KB) -- this citation is truly dead, not a false negative. I could not find this PDF mirrored anywhere (archive.org's availability API rate-limited my checks; no cached copy located), so I cannot verify or replace the 1999 start year, the 1015mm diameter value, or the Gazli fuel-source attribution from any source right now. Second, I checked whether any OTHER, live, independent source supports 1999 or 1015mm for a 'Line II' entity: none does. The only concrete, dated, independently-verifiable event on this exact corridor's second stage is the 2016-2017 Kyrgyz-section reconstruction (construction from October 2016 per vesti.kg; commissioned 2017-08-29 per BOTH neftegaz.ru and ru.sputnik.kg independently) -- nothing in any source I found points to 1999. Notably, this row's Capacity=3.9 bcm/y is an EXACT, to-the-decimal match for neftegaz.ru's explicit statement that post-upgrade throughput at the Chuy metering station rose to '3,9 млрд м3/год' -- i.e. whoever originally populated this row's Capacity almost certainly used the 2017 event, which directly conflicts with the same row's StartYear1=1999 sourced (nominally) from the 2013 academic PDF. Third, on Length: I checked the GEM-drawn route itself is documented (via RouteNotes, sheet-side, not something I'm citing) as 'parallel to Pipeline I' at RouteType=Mapped/RouteAccuracy=high -- i.e. the original researcher (NF) intentionally drew a second, corridor-length parallel route, which is internally consistent with Length=1585.00 IF the intent is a genuine second full-length string. But none of the three independently-verified 2016-2017 news sources describe a new FULL 1,585 km second pipe -- they describe a partial reconstruction confined to ~111-112 km inside Kyrgyzstan (vesti.kg's km-post description: corridor markers 1001-1113; ru.sputnik.kg: '111 километров магистрали' reconstructed through Kyrgyzstan). If Length=1585.00 is meant to describe that same 2016-2017 project, it is wrong by roughly 14x. If instead Length=1585.00 correctly describes an actual, separate, full-corridor second string dating to 1999 that I simply couldn't verify because its only citation is dead, then the row's Capacity value is instead the one that's misattributed (borrowing a later, unrelated 2017 event's number onto an older entity). Either way, the row currently mixes numbers from what look like two different historical events onto one line, and I cannot responsibly pick a winner without the dead source restored or a fresh primary source located -- flagging as an unresolved internal-consistency defect rather than silently 'fixing' one field. On Diameter='720, 1015' specifically: I found no live source (including two separate 2017 sputnik.kg articles I checked verbatim for '1015'/'1016') stating this pipe's diameter; leaving it unresolved rather than force a match. NB: 720mm alone is separately, independently corroborated for the OVERALL corridor by vesti.kg (2017), but that same 720mm value is also already claimed by sibling row P0739/Line I, so it does not distinguish 'Line II' as a separate pipe run.

summary: P5810 (BGR-TBA 'Line II'/2nd string) is a real, independently-confirmed entity (3 independent Russian/Kyrgyz sources on the 2016-2017 Kyrgyz-section capacity upgrade, Capacity=3.9 matching neftegaz.ru to the decimal) -- NOT a duplicate/phantom of sibling P0739 -- but staged 3 concerns: (1) spec/internal-consistency -- Length=1585.00 and StartYear1=1999 rest solely on a now-dead citation (library.tou.edu.kz PDF, confirmed genuine HTTP 404) and conflict with the row's own best-evidenced field (Capacity, tied to a 2017 event, not 1999 or a full 1,585 km second pipe); (2) attribution -- EndCountryOrArea='Kyrgyzstan' is wrong, should be 'Kazakhstan' (Almaty is a Kazakh city; sibling P0739 already has this right); (3) existence/classification confirmed with caveat.
